objective: Correctly preserve CPVS internal source identifiers from Table2 Seq and independently verify ID-to-ZTF-name identity against the published reference.
previous_knowledge_consumed: Official VizieR ReadMe J/ApJS/249/18 defines Table2 bytes 1-22 as the ZTF object name and bytes 24-29 as Seq, the internal source identifier; the photometry files use Seq.
The existing derivation parser ignored the Seq field and assigned one-based row ordinals as SourceIDs.
Official VizieR ReadMe J/ApJ/932/118 defines Table4 ID as a catalog internal identifier with range 1-781604.
The paper states its 730184-object subset contains at least one 2.5-sigma g-band and 3-sigma r-band detection.
The numeric CPVS reconstruction mismatch has been reported as 741786 candidates versus 730184 published IDs; exact reconstruction remains unresolved.

baseline.status: The parent ID parser uses row ordinals instead of the documented Table2 Seq/internal SourceID. This PR corrects identifier interpretation only; selection thresholds and frozen v0.2.0/v1.0.1 artifacts remain unchanged.

expected_improvement: Read the explicit Seq/internal SourceID from Table2 rows when present, retaining row-ordinal fallback only for simplified legacy fixtures.
Add regression coverage for non-contiguous internal IDs so row order cannot silently replace SourceID.
Audit actual Table2 SourceID-to-ZTF-name mapping against published Table4 ID/name pairs.
Report numeric-ID and object-name membership separately in the heavy source-backed artifact.

correctness.before: Source IDs from catalog rows were replaced by sequential row ordinals.
correctness.after: Official Table2 Seq identifiers are preserved and independently cross-checked against published Table4 IDs and ZTF names.

reproducibility.before: No explicit regression for sparse/non-contiguous internal source identifiers.
reproducibility.after: Regression tests cover explicit Seq parsing and identity cross-match diagnostics.

evidence: Official source schema directly documents the Seq field and its internal identifier role.
Production parser, regression tests, name-based audit script, workflow invocation, and this lifecycle record are included in PR #194.
validation.blocker: Focused tests and full heavy source-backed validation must pass; the 11602 candidate-only discrepancy remains unresolved until the corrected mapping produces and independently verifies a reproducible result.

findings: A concrete identifier-mapping defect exists: the production parser assigned row ordinals instead of reading the official Table2 Seq/internal SourceID field.
Whether this defect fully explains the previously reported 11602 candidate-only discrepancy is not yet established; the corrected full-data run and independent object-name audit must determine that.
Do not replace an explicit internal object identifier with row ordinal when the source schema provides an identifier column.
The CPVS paper's stated detection criterion must remain separate from catalog summary-field diagnostics.
Exact numeric membership is not accepted as proof of correct object identity until ID-to-name mapping is validated.

open_blockers: Run the focused source-ID and object-identity tests plus full CI.
Complete the heavy source-backed workflow using the corrected Seq mapping.
Review the candidate/reference ID and ZTF-name membership counts; do not claim scientific resolution without exact, reproducible agreement or a documented remaining cause.

knowledge_carried_forward: Preserve actual Table2 Seq/internal SourceID values.
Do not tune thresholds or add unrelated catalog summary-field filters to force 730184.
Keep CPVS exact reconstruction unresolved until corrected source-backed evidence is reviewed.
Do not change the frozen v0.2.0 baseline or v1.0.1 release artifacts.
